title: UCAT (University Clinical Aptitude Test)
content_provenance: Original practice items authored from the public UCAT test specifications. Not a capture of past test questions.

items.stem: Passage - For a decade the city has encouraged rooftop beekeeping to help pollinators. Ecologists reply that honeybees are managed livestock rather than wild pollinators, and that dense hives can outcompete solitary wild bees for the nectar available in city parks. Which of the following can be properly inferred from the passage?
options: Rooftop hives produce more honey than rural hives do
The beekeeping campaign may not help the wild pollinators it was meant to support
Solitary bees are more popular with residents than honeybees are
The city will end its beekeeping programme next year
items.explanation: The passage contrasts managed honeybees with wild pollinators and warns that hives may crowd out wild bees, so the campaign may fail to help them; the other options are unsupported.

items.stem: Passage - A railway operator claims that adding a second nightly service cut delays, noting that average delay fell from 18 minutes to 7 minutes in the following quarter. Which statement, if true, most undermines the operator's claim?
options: The new service runs between the same two cities as the original one
Freight traffic, a well known cause of disruption, fell sharply that quarter after an unrelated rerouting
Some trains were cancelled during that quarter
Passenger numbers rose during that quarter
items.explanation: A sharp fall in freight traffic supplies a rival cause for the shorter delays, so the improvement need not be due to the extra service, which weakens the claim.

items.stem: Passage - Critics say the new library is a luxury the town cannot afford. The librarian replies that last year the library handled 12,000 job applications submitted on its public computers. The reference to job applications serves to
options: estimate how many books the library lends each year
accept that the library is a luxury
show that the library performs an essential service beyond lending books
prove that unemployment in the town is unusually high
items.explanation: The librarian answers the luxury charge by naming a vital service the library provides, so the reference functions as a defence of the library's wider value.

items.stem: Passage - Some predict that remote work will empty city centres. Yet office data show that most firms now lease smaller floors while keeping a city base for meetings and training, so weekday footfall has fallen by a fifth rather than collapsed. The main point of the passage is that
options: firms should move their offices out to rural areas
city centres have become unprofitable for every business
remote work has reduced activity in city centres without ending it
meetings and training are no longer useful to firms
items.explanation: The passage accepts a fall in footfall but rejects collapse, so its main point is reduction rather than elimination; the other choices overstate or distort it.

items.stem: Passage - The council planted 3,000 street trees in 2023 and reported that 92 percent survived their first summer. It also reported that planting was paid from a reserve fund rather than council tax and that maintenance now falls to a contractor. Which of the following is not stated in the passage?
options: How many of the surviving trees were native species
Where the money for the planting came from
Who is responsible for the trees now
What proportion of the trees lived through the summer
items.explanation: The passage gives the funding source, the maintenance responsibility and the survival rate, but says nothing about native species, so that is the detail not stated.

items.stem: Passage - A doctor argues that walking groups will ease loneliness more cheaply than medication alone, citing a pilot in which 60 volunteers joined weekly walks and reported fewer lonely days after three months. Which finding would most strengthen the doctor's argument?
options: Most of the volunteers had already been walking for exercise before the pilot
The cost per volunteer of the walking groups was lower than the cost of the medication those same volunteers had previously taken
The pilot ran for six months rather than for three months
Some volunteers stopped attending the walks before the pilot ended
items.explanation: Evidence that walking really did cost less per person than the medication supports both halves of the claim about loneliness and cost, while the other findings are incidental.

items.stem: Passage - An editor claims that the newspaper lost subscribers because delivery moved from Saturday to Monday, citing a 12 percent fall in subscriptions over the three months after the change. The editor's claim assumes which of the following?
options: Saturday was the delivery day used by every newspaper in the country
Subscription figures are published every quarter
Nothing else that affects subscriptions changed during those three months
Most subscribers read the paper on the day it is delivered
items.explanation: Attributing the whole fall to the schedule change requires that no other factor moved subscriptions at the same time, which is the assumption the argument needs.

items.stem: Passage - Salt marshes lock away carbon up to ten times faster per hectare than forests, yet they are drained for agriculture at a rate unmatched in any other ecosystem. It follows that
options: farming on drained marshes always fails to produce a crop
forests should be cut down so that marshes can be restored
carbon storage is the only service that marshes provide
the ecosystems best at storing carbon are not the best protected ones
items.explanation: Very high carbon storage alongside unusually heavy destruction supports the conclusion that the most efficient stores are poorly protected; the other statements do not follow.

items.stem: Passage - The road widening plan is, the author concedes, well intentioned and its engineers are certainly competent. Still, the author writes, a scheme that adds lanes without adding buses treats congestion as something to make room for rather than something to reduce. The author's attitude toward the plan is best described as
options: respectful of the people behind it but opposed to its underlying logic
enthusiastic about every element of the design
dismissive of the engineers' professional ability
indifferent to whether the plan goes ahead
items.explanation: The author praises the intention and the engineers yet rejects the lane first approach, giving a mixed attitude of respect for the people and opposition to the reasoning.

items.stem: Passage - A clinic moved to online booking and saw missed appointments fall by only 3 percent, while neighbouring clinics reported falls of a quarter or more after the same switch. Which of the following best explains the difference?
options: Online booking was introduced in the same month at every clinic involved
The neighbouring clinics had previously required patients to telephone at peak times, whereas this clinic had long offered an out-of-hours answering service
The clinic's building provides parking spaces for its patients
The clinic treats both children and adults
items.explanation: If the neighbouring clinics had a worse telephone system beforehand, they had far more room to improve, which explains why their falls in missed appointments were larger.

items.stem: Passage - Between 2019 and 2024 the number of electric vans registered in the region rose from 400 to 5,200, while the total number of vans on the road rose by 8 percent. Charging points available to commercial drivers rose from 60 to 210. Which conclusion is best supported?
options: Electric vans now make up most of the region's van fleet
The region has more charging points than any neighbouring region
Growth in electric vans has outpaced the growth in charging provision for them
The charging points were built mainly for private car drivers
items.explanation: Electric vans rose thirteenfold while charge points rose only about three and a half times, so provision lagged adoption; the other claims need information the passage does not give.

items.stem: Passage - A school reports that pupils who eat school lunches score higher on attention tests than pupils who bring food from home. The report then notes that families who prepare lunch at home are on average poorer than families who buy school lunches. The final sentence serves to
options: show that school lunches offer better value than home lunches
prove that school lunches caused the higher attention scores
explain how the attention tests were marked
suggest a possible alternative explanation for the difference in scores
items.explanation: Introducing family income raises a confounding factor that could produce the score gap, so the sentence weakens rather than proves the causal reading of the results.

items.stem: Passage - Cycle lanes take space from parked cars, and parked cars bring shoppers, so traders fear lost trade. Yet a study of eleven high streets found that sales per metre of frontage rose after lanes were built, and deliveries could still be made in side streets. Which statement best expresses the passage's main conclusion?
options: Worry that cycle lanes reduce trade is not borne out by the evidence
Traders should never be consulted about road schemes
Parked cars contribute nothing to a high street
Every high street in the country should build a cycle lane
items.explanation: The rising sales and the workable deliveries are offered to reject the traders' fear, so the first option is the main conclusion and the others overreach the passage.

items.stem: Passage - Every property inspected by the surveyor was either rated above average or flagged for urgent repair, and no property rated above average was flagged for urgent repair. If the surveyor inspected Willow House, which of the following must be true?
options: Willow House was rated above average
Willow House received exactly one of the two labels
Willow House was inspected a second time
Properties rated below average were never inspected
items.explanation: Each inspected property receives at least one label and no property receives both, so Willow House must have exactly one; the other statements do not follow from the premises.

items.stem: Passage - A council wants to cut bus fares to 1 pound and argues that the resulting rise in passenger numbers will leave fare revenue unchanged. Which evidence would most support the council's argument?
options: Bus operating costs have risen in each of the last five years
The council did not raise council tax this year
Similar fare cuts elsewhere raised passenger numbers by a greater percentage than the percentage cut in fares
Most bus passengers in the region are students
items.explanation: Revenue holds only if the percentage rise in passengers outweighs the percentage cut in fare, and evidence from comparable cuts bears directly on that link.

items.stem: All pharmacists at the practice have completed the vaccination module, and everyone who completed the vaccination module has given at least one flu vaccination. No one who has given a flu vaccination works only evenings. Which conclusion must follow for staff at the practice?
options: Every member of staff at the practice is a pharmacist
Only pharmacists have ever given a flu vaccination
The vaccination module is compulsory for every member of staff
No pharmacist at the practice works only evenings
items.explanation: Pharmacists completed the module, so they have given a flu vaccination, and anyone who has given one cannot work only evenings; the other statements go beyond the premises.

items.stem: A hospital committee must choose between two triage software packages. Package Alpha costs more but has been used in three nearby trusts with no recorded safety incidents. Package Beta costs half as much but has been piloted for only two months in a single clinic. Which consideration should weigh most heavily in the decision?
options: The longer safety record of Package Alpha, because patient safety cannot be traded against cost
The lower price of Package Beta, because the trust has a fixed annual budget
The fact that Package Beta was piloted locally, because local trials are easier to monitor
The number of features each package advertises in its brochure
items.explanation: In triage software a failure can harm patients directly, so a proven safety record outranks price, convenience and marketing claims in the decision.

items.stem: A town proposes closing its two smaller libraries and spending the saving on one large library with longer opening hours. A councillor objects that the nearest bus route to the new site runs only twice a day. Which of the following best shows why the councillor's objection damages the proposal?
options: Buses cost more to run than small libraries do to keep open
Residents without cars who now walk to a local library may lose practical access to any library
The larger library will need more staff than the two smaller ones
Twice daily bus services are common in rural areas
items.explanation: If people who rely on walking or infrequent buses cannot reach the new site, the merger removes service from those who most need it, which is the force of the objection.

items.stem: A study of 200 office workers found that those who took a full lunch break away from their desk reported less afternoon fatigue than those who ate at their desks, and that the difference was largest among workers who walked during the break. Which conclusion is best supported by the study?
options: Eating at a desk causes fatigue in most workers
Every worker should take a lunch break of at least one hour
Walking during a lunch break may contribute to lower afternoon fatigue
Fatigue reduces the productivity of office workers
items.explanation: The largest difference appearing among walkers supports an association between walking at lunch and lower fatigue, while the study does not prove causation or justify the sweeping claims.

items.stem: In a sixth form, every student who plays rugby also plays a sport, no student who plays a sport is in the school choir, and some students who do not play rugby are in the choir. Which statement must be true?
options: Every student who plays rugby is in the choir
Some students who play a sport are in the choir
Every student in the choir plays rugby
Some students in the choir do not play a sport
items.explanation: Choir membership rules out playing a sport, and at least one choir member does not play rugby, so some choir members certainly do not play a sport.

items.stem: A clinic can fund either a new ultrasound machine or two extra nurse practitioners for a year. Waiting lists for scans are 14 weeks, while patients usually wait 9 days to see a nurse and can be seen the next day in an emergency. Which consideration is most important in deciding between the two options?
options: Whether the scan waiting list is delaying diagnosis for conditions that can worsen quickly
Whether the ultrasound machine would be the most expensive item the clinic has bought
Whether two nurses are easier to replace than one machine
Whether patients prefer machines to people
items.explanation: The decisive question is clinical risk, and a long scan delay matters most where waiting risks harm, whereas cost, replaceability and preference are secondary.

items.stem: A retailer argues that it should not be required to offer a delivery service, because customers who want delivery can use the many couriers now operating in the town. Which assumption does the argument rely on?
options: The retailer has never offered a delivery service in the past
Couriers can collect from the retailer's premises in a way that actually serves its customers
Courier prices are lower than the retailer's own delivery charges would be
Most customers in the town prefer to shop online
items.explanation: The alternative only works if couriers can realistically collect and deliver for these customers, so without that assumption the argument collapses; price comparison is not required.

items.stem: A booking system grants a refund when the ticket is flexible or the train was cancelled by the operator, and it grants a free seat change when the ticket is flexible or the delay exceeded 30 minutes. Jody's train was cancelled and Jody's ticket is not flexible. Which outcomes apply to Jody?
options: Both a refund and a free seat change apply
A free seat change applies but a refund does not
A refund applies but a free seat change does not
Neither outcome applies
items.explanation: Cancellation alone satisfies the refund condition, while a seat change needs flexibility or a delay over 30 minutes and neither is given, so only the refund applies.

items.stem: A council measured recycling in two districts. District A introduced weekly collections and its recycling rate rose from 24 percent to 31 percent. District B introduced weekly collections at the same time and its rate rose from 30 percent to 33 percent. Which conclusion is best supported?
options: District A now recycles more waste in total than District B
Weekly collections are the only cause of the rise in both districts
District B's residents recycle less than District A's residents
The rise from weekly collections was larger where the starting rate was lower
items.explanation: District A rose by 7 points from a lower base and District B by only 3 points from a higher one, so the gain was larger where the starting rate was lower; the rest are unsupported.

items.stem: A hospital is choosing a new electronic patient record system. The board is told that System One has a five year safety record, that System Two is cheaper to run, and that System Two has not been used in any UK hospital of comparable size. Which missing piece of information is most important before a decision is made?
options: Whether System Two has been tested in hospitals of a similar size, and what the results were
How many years each system's supplier has been in business
Whether the board members have used a computer before
Which system has the more attractive user interface
items.explanation: The stated gap is exactly the untested setting, so evidence from comparable hospitals would resolve the main risk; supplier age, board experience and appearance do not.

items.stem: Either the theatre will close or the council will raise the levy, and the council will raise the levy only if the budget shortfall is confirmed. The budget shortfall has not been confirmed. What follows?
options: The council will raise the levy
The theatre will close
The budget shortfall will be confirmed later
The theatre will stay open
items.explanation: An unconfirmed shortfall rules out raising the levy, and since one of the two things must happen, the remaining possibility is that the theatre closes.

items.stem: A school must decide whether to make its walks-to-school scheme compulsory. Supporters say it would cut congestion at the gate, while opponents note that some pupils live more than three miles away and some have mobility conditions. Which response best answers the objection while keeping the scheme?
options: Make the scheme compulsory for every pupil regardless of distance
Cancel the scheme until congestion at the gate becomes worse
Require all parents to sign a petition supporting the scheme
Apply the requirement to pupils living within one mile and offer exemptions on medical grounds
items.explanation: Limiting the rule to those who can walk and adding a medical exemption removes both stated objections while preserving the scheme, unlike the blanket, cancel or petition options.

items.stem: A developer argues that a new supermarket will create 120 jobs, so the planning application should be approved. Which of the following is the strongest objection to the developer's argument?
options: Supermarkets are large buildings that change the look of a street
Some residents do not want to work in a supermarket
The developer has built supermarkets in other towns before
The jobs may be part time and may replace jobs lost when existing shops close
items.explanation: Net job creation is the whole basis of the argument, so evidence that the gains are temporary or offset by closures strikes at that basis rather than at appearance or history.

items.stem: Three clinics offer the same minor procedure. Clinic North charges 240 per patient with a 2 week wait, Clinic South charges 180 with a 9 week wait, and Clinic East charges 210 with a 4 week wait. The board decides on the shortest wait among clinics charging 210 or less. Which clinic is selected?
options: Clinic East, because it has the shortest wait among the clinics charging 210 or less
Clinic South, because it has the lowest charge overall
Clinic North, because it has the shortest wait overall
No clinic, because every clinic fails the cost limit
items.explanation: Only South and East fall within the 210 limit, and East's 4 week wait beats South's 9 weeks, so East satisfies the rule; North fails the cost limit.

items.stem: No prescription only medicine is sold without a pharmacist's supervision, some health supplements are sold without a pharmacist's supervision, and all prescription only medicines are regulated by the board. Which statement must be true?
options: All health supplements are regulated by the board
Some health supplements are not prescription only medicines
Nothing sold with supervision is a health supplement
The board regulates every product sold in the pharmacy
items.explanation: Any product sold without supervision cannot be a prescription only medicine, and some supplements are sold that way, so at least some supplements fall outside that category.

items.stem: A gym recorded visits on four days, with Monday 170, Tuesday 150, Wednesday 180 and Thursday 210. The gym counts a day as busy when it records more than 160 visits. What proportion of the four days were busy?
options: One quarter
One half
Three quarters
Four fifths
items.explanation: Monday, Wednesday and Thursday all exceed 160 while Tuesday does not, giving three busy days out of four, which is three quarters.

items.stem: A pharmacy dispensed 800 prescriptions in January and 960 prescriptions in February. What was the percentage increase in prescriptions dispensed from January to February?
options: 16 percent
150 percent
160 percent
20 percent
items.explanation: The rise is 160 prescriptions, and 160 divided by the original 800 is one fifth, which is a 20 percent increase rather than 16 or 160 percent.

items.stem: Five ward clerks logged these numbers of annual leave days, 12, 15, 9, 24 and 10. What is the mean number of leave days taken by the five clerks?
options: 14 days
12 days
15 days
10 days
items.explanation: The five values total 70 days, and 70 divided by 5 gives a mean of 14 days; the other figures ignore either the total or the count of clerks.

items.stem: A triage line handled 450 calls in 6 hours on Monday and 600 calls in 8 hours on Tuesday. What is the difference between the average number of calls per hour on the two days?
options: Tuesday was higher by 10 calls per hour
There is no difference, because both averages are 75 calls per hour
Monday was higher by 15 calls per hour
Tuesday was higher by 150 calls per hour
items.explanation: 450 divided by 6 is 75 calls per hour and 600 divided by 8 is also 75, so the two daily averages are identical and the difference is zero.

items.stem: In a clinic, patients are assigned in the ratio of 3 nurses' patients to 5 doctors' patients, and there are 240 patients in total. How many patients are assigned to nurses?
options: 75 patients
80 patients
90 patients
150 patients
items.explanation: The ratio gives 8 parts in total, so each part is 30 patients, and the nurses' 3 parts are 3 times 30, which is 90 patients.

items.stem: A survey of 400 patients recorded how they contacted their practice, with 160 by phone, 120 by app, 60 by email and 60 in person. What percentage of the patients used the app?
options: 12 percent
24 percent
40 percent
30 percent
items.explanation: 120 app users out of 400 is 120 divided by 400, which is 0.3, so the app share is 30 percent; the other figures use the wrong totals.

items.stem: A ward buys disinfectant in 5 litre bottles costing 18 pounds each, and the ward uses 0.75 litres each day. How many whole bottles are needed for a 30 day period, and what do they cost?
options: 5 bottles costing 90 pounds
4 bottles costing 72 pounds
5 bottles costing 72 pounds
6 bottles costing 90 pounds
items.explanation: 30 days at 0.75 litres needs 22.5 litres, and 22.5 divided by 5 is 4.5 bottles, so 5 whole bottles are required at 18 pounds each, giving 90 pounds.

items.stem: Four community clinics saw these patient numbers in one week, North 220, South 180, East 260 and West 140. What is the mean number of patients seen per clinic that week?
options: 180 patients
200 patients
220 patients
260 patients
items.explanation: The four figures total 800 patients, and 800 divided by 4 clinics gives a mean of 200 patients per clinic.

items.stem: A waiting list of 320 patients was reduced by 15 percent in a single month. How many patients remained on the list after that month?
options: 268 patients
270 patients
272 patients
288 patients
items.explanation: 15 percent of 320 is 48 patients, and 320 minus 48 leaves 272 patients on the list; the other figures apply the percentage incorrectly.

items.stem: A community nurse travels 60 kilometres to a patient's home in 45 minutes and returns by a longer route of 75 kilometres in 50 minutes. What are the average speeds for the outward and return legs?
options: 80 and 75 kilometres per hour
75 and 80 kilometres per hour
60 and 75 kilometres per hour
80 and 90 kilometres per hour
items.explanation: 45 minutes is 0.75 hours, so 60 divided by 0.75 is 80 kilometres per hour, and 50 minutes is five sixths of an hour, so 75 divided by that is 90 kilometres per hour.

items.stem: Of 500 appointments at a clinic, 60 percent were kept, 10 percent were cancelled by the clinic, and the remainder were missed by patients. How many appointments were missed by patients?
options: 150 appointments
100 appointments
50 appointments
200 appointments
items.explanation: Kept appointments total 300 and clinic cancellations total 50, leaving 500 minus 350, which is 150 appointments missed by patients.

items.stem: Service A charges a fixed fee of 250 pounds plus 4 pounds for each patient seen, and Service B charges a fixed fee of 120 pounds plus 9 pounds for each patient seen. For how many patients do the two services cost the same amount?
options: 25 patients
26 patients
30 patients
39 patients
items.explanation: Setting the totals equal gives 250 plus 4p equals 120 plus 9p, so 130 equals 5p and p is 26 patients, where both services cost 354 pounds.

items.stem: A clinic's did-not-attend rate fell from 8 percent of appointments to 5 percent of appointments. What is the relative reduction in the did-not-attend rate?
options: 3 percent
5 percent
37.5 percent
62.5 percent
items.explanation: The fall is 3 percentage points on a starting rate of 8 percent, and 3 divided by 8 is 0.375, so the relative reduction is 37.5 percent rather than 3 percent.

items.stem: A hospital has three wards with 24, 32 and 40 beds, and each ward's cleaning team covers one bed for every two staff per shift. How many cleaning staff are needed per shift across all three wards?
options: 24 staff
36 staff
96 staff
48 staff
items.explanation: The wards hold 96 beds in total, and at one bed for every two staff the requirement is 96 divided by 2, which is 48 staff per shift.

items.stem: A pharmacy buys a box of 120 gloves for 36 pounds, and the box holds 60 pairs of gloves which the pharmacy sells at 1.50 pounds per pair. What is the profit on one box if every pair is sold?
options: 54 pounds
36 pounds
60 pounds
90 pounds
items.explanation: Sixty pairs at 1.50 pounds brings in 90 pounds, and subtracting the 36 pound cost of the box leaves a profit of 54 pounds.

items.stem: As a first year healthcare assistant you notice that a senior colleague has left the controlled drug register unsigned after giving morphine to a patient. What is the most appropriate course of action?
options: Do nothing, because the colleague is senior and the register is not your responsibility
Tell several colleagues so that everyone on the unit is aware of what happened
Speak to the senior colleague privately, explain the documentation requirement and complete a factual incident report
Sign the register yourself to show that the drug was properly recorded
items.explanation: Raising the gap privately and promptly with a factual report addresses the record without gossip or falsification, which are the least defensible responses.

items.stem: At the end of a clinic a patient asks you to explain a complex discharge letter, but their interpreter has left and your shift ends in five minutes. Which response is the least appropriate?
options: Arrange an interpreter by telephone before the patient leaves the building
Offer to book a follow-up appointment with an interpreter present
Explain that you will arrange an interpreter and give the patient the letter to take home
Read the whole letter aloud quickly so that the patient has something before they leave
items.explanation: Explaining complex clinical information without a competent interpreter risks serious misunderstanding, so a rushed reading is the least appropriate of the choices.

items.stem: You overhear a colleague giving details of another patient's test results to a patient in a busy open waiting area. What is the most appropriate immediate action?
options: Speak to your colleague straight away and move the conversation to a private area
Report the colleague to their regulator at the end of the day
Do nothing, because you did not catch the other patient's name
Mention it to other staff at the next team meeting
items.explanation: Stopping the disclosure at once and moving it somewhere private limits the ongoing breach, whereas waiting, staying silent or deferring it lets the exposure continue.

items.stem: A patient recovering well offers you a 100 pound voucher as thanks for your care during a long admission. What is the most appropriate response?
options: Accept the voucher, because the patient has already been discharged
Decline politely, explain that gifts of that kind are not permitted, and suggest a written comment to the ward team
Accept the voucher and share it with the rest of the team
Decline the voucher but accept an invitation to a family meal
items.explanation: A clear, courteous refusal with a suggested alternative keeps the boundary of professional honesty intact, while every other option still crosses it.

items.stem: You realise that a dressing was changed on the wrong leg and that the correct leg has now been left undressed overnight, and the patient has noticed. What is the most appropriate action?
options: Say nothing, because the patient has not come to any harm
Blame the agency nurse who handed over the shift
Tell the patient what happened honestly, apologise, inform the nurse in charge and record the incident
Change the dressing quietly and mention it at the next handover
items.explanation: Open disclosure, an apology, escalation and documentation together meet the duties to the patient and the organisation; silence and blame do not.

items.stem: An adult patient with a learning disability attends clinic with a carer who answers every question and refuses to leave the room. Which action is the least appropriate?
options: Ask to speak with the patient alone using a calm and unpressured approach
Record your own observations of the patient's communication with the carer absent
Discuss your concerns with the practice safeguarding lead
Accept the carer's answers without question in order to avoid causing offence
items.explanation: Taking every answer from the carer removes the patient's own voice and could hide coercion or harm, making it the least appropriate option here.

items.stem: A patient asks you not to tell their GP about a condition you have discussed, but the condition affects their ability to drive safely. What is the most appropriate course of action?
options: Explain that you have a duty to share information where there is a risk to public safety, and tell the patient exactly what you will share and with whom
Keep the information secret, because the patient asked you to
Tell the whole team so that everyone can watch out for the patient
Wait until the patient's next appointment and ask them again then
items.explanation: A risk to other road users overrides confidentiality, and the patient should be told what will be shared and why, rather than the matter being hidden or broadcast.

items.stem: A relative of a patient is shouting at reception staff about a delayed appointment and is preventing other patients from being heard. What is the most appropriate action?
options: Ask security to remove the relative from the building immediately
Ask the relative to move to a quieter area with you, listen to the concern and explain what can be done about the delay
Ignore the behaviour so that the clinic keeps to its schedule
Tell the relative that their behaviour is unacceptable and walk away
items.explanation: Moving the conversation, listening and explaining addresses the concern while protecting other patients, and it de-escalates rather than provokes or avoids the issue.

items.stem: You notice that a colleague has been arriving late, smelling of alcohol and making frequent mistakes during night shifts. What is the most appropriate course of action?
options: Gossip about the behaviour with other staff during the break
Wait to see whether the pattern continues over the next few weeks
Raise your concerns with the colleague directly and, if you remain worried, report them to your manager so the issue can be handled supportively
Tell the patient's family so that they can raise a complaint
items.explanation: Patient safety and the colleague's wellbeing both require early, proportionate escalation through the proper channel rather than gossip, delay or involving patients' families.

items.stem: Two patients need the last appointment of the day. One needs a routine review, while the other reports new chest pain. Which course of action is the least appropriate?
options: Triage the patient with new chest pain for immediate assessment
Ask an on-call clinician to assess the patient with chest pain today
Deal with the chest pain now and book the routine review for another day
Offer the appointment to whoever arrived first, because queue order is fair
items.explanation: Applying a simple queue rule when one patient may have a time critical condition ignores clinical urgency, which makes it the least appropriate choice.

items.stem: A member of staff has posted a photograph of a hospital corridor on a personal social media account, and a patient's whiteboard is clearly visible in the background. What is the most appropriate action?
options: Ask them to remove the image immediately and report the breach through the usual incidents process
Report the member of staff directly to their professional regulator
Do nothing, because no patient's face is visible in the photograph
Post a public comment telling them that they have broken the rules
items.explanation: Removing the image limits the exposure and an internal report handles the breach proportionately, while regulator action or public shaming is disproportionate and doing nothing ignores the identifiable details.

items.stem: During a handover you are told that a patient's allergy status is unknown and the prescription is ready to be given. What is the most appropriate action before the medicine is administered?
options: Give the medicine, because the prescription has already been signed
Check the patient's records and, if it is still unclear, speak to the prescriber before administering anything
Ask the patient in passing whether they have any allergies and record whatever they say
Hand the prescription to a more senior colleague and say nothing
items.explanation: Verifying the record and escalating to the prescriber if doubt remains is the safest route before administration, whereas relying on a rushed question or staying silent is not.

items.stem: A patient complains that they were kept waiting for 90 minutes and says they intend to post about the experience online. Which response is the least appropriate?
options: Apologise for the wait and explain the reason for the delay
Explain the practice's complaints procedure and give the patient the details
Offer the patient a small cash payment if they agree not to post anything online
Take the patient's contact details and arrange for a manager to call them
items.explanation: Offering money in exchange for silence attempts to buy off a legitimate complaint and damages trust, so it is far less appropriate than apologising, explaining or escalating.

items.stem: A student nurse asks you to sign off a competency that you have not actually seen them complete. What is the most appropriate response?
options: Sign the form, because the student seems confident in the skill
Sign the form and ask them to demonstrate the skill to you later
Refuse to sign and report the student for dishonesty
Explain that you can only sign for skills you have witnessed, and offer to supervise them through the skill so that it can be signed afterwards
items.explanation: Honesty about what was observed plus a constructive plan to supervise the skill protects both the student and future patients, unlike signing early or reporting immediately.

items.stem: A patient with capacity disagrees with their care plan, and their family are demanding clinical details that the patient has asked not to be shared. What is the most appropriate action?
options: Confirm the patient's wishes about information sharing, explain the limits of confidentiality to the family and offer a meeting with the clinical team
Give the family the clinical details, because they are the next of kin
Refuse to speak to the family at all about any aspect of the care
Ask the family to make a formal complaint before any discussion takes place
items.explanation: The competent patient decides what is shared, while the family are still offered information and a meeting within those limits, which respects both confidentiality and the relationship.
